# clovapi

> Great models, within reach. A shared model API network with direct consumer access and optional open-source contribution nodes.

clovapi lets consumers discover and call models supplied by online contribution nodes and platform capacity through one authenticated `/v1` API. Consumers do not need to install the CLI, configure an upstream, or contribute capacity first. Contributors can run the open-source CLI to connect resources they are authorized to share while keeping upstream credentials on the node.

Current status:

- The console provides email verification, server-side sessions, account-scoped data, hashed consumer API credentials, online model discovery, and contribution-node controls.
- Full API credentials are shown once when created; only a hash and display prefix are stored.
- The model gateway, persistent contribution-node connections, request routing, streaming responses, and request-count limits are active.
- Credit settlement and free allowance grants are not enabled. Connecting an API or staying online does not currently earn credits.
- Platform capacity does not guarantee every model, continuous availability, or unlimited usage.

Available software:

The open-source clovapi CLI runs contribution nodes, stores provider profiles and upstream credentials locally, syncs available model IDs, and transcodes OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini-compatible API formats. Consumers do not need it. A standalone local proxy remains available as an advanced mode.

- Home: /en and /zh-CN

- Local model API proxy guide: /en/blog/local-model-api-proxy

- Agent-readable skill source: /skill.md
- GitHub: https://github.com/joohw/clovapi
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clovapi/cli

Shared API:

- https://clovapi.com/v1/models
- https://clovapi.com/v1/chat/completions
- https://clovapi.com/v1/responses

Primary topics:

- shared model API access with one platform credential
- discovering models currently supplied by online nodes
- contributing authorized API capacity through an open-source node
- platform and node request-count limits
- secure email authentication and API credential management
- contribution-node credential boundaries and request routing
- advanced local LLM API proxy
- OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini API format conversion
- Codex and Claude subscription access through localhost
- local request logs, usage inspection, and provider routing
